title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #12

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a percussion instrument? (1 mark)
   A. Whistle
   B. Trumpet
   C. Drum
   D. Recorder

2. A thumb piano produces sound when you (1 mark)
   A. blow into it
   B. pluck its metal tongues with your thumbs
   C. rub its skin
   D. hit it with a big stick

3. What does the drumhead do when it is struck? (1 mark)
   A. It holds the drum stand
   B. It vibrates and makes the sound
   C. It cools the drum
   D. It stays completely still

4. On a xylophone, the long bars give (1 mark)
   A. low notes
   B. only clapping sounds
   C. no sound
   D. high notes

5. Which is the beater of a drum? (1 mark)
   A. The rope
   B. The stick or hand that strikes it
   C. The skin
   D. The shell

6. The basic knot for the macramé ball is the (1 mark)
   A. sailor's knot
   B. reef knot
   C. fisherman's bend
   D. overhand knot

7. What do the letters GK stand for? (1 mark)
   A. Goal Keeper
   B. Great Kicker
   C. Goal Kicker
   D. Goal King

8. What is the minimum distance a defender must keep from the player with the ball? (1 mark)
   A. 0.9 metres
   B. 5 metres
   C. 1 centimetre
   D. 10 metres

9. Which is an improvised glue? (1 mark)
   A. Paint thinner
   B. Flour paste
   C. Salt water
   D. Engine oil

10. What do you add to a colour to make it darker? (1 mark)
   A. White
   B. Yellow
   C. Water only
   D. Black

11. What do you add to a colour to make it lighter? (1 mark)
   A. More of the same colour only
   B. Soil
   C. Black
   D. White

12. How long does a crotchet rest last? (1 mark)
   A. Two beats
   B. Half a beat
   C. No time
   D. One beat

13. Which is a quality of a good rhythmic pattern? (1 mark)
   A. Variation of note values
   B. Only one kind of note
   C. No beat
   D. Ending on a rest always

14. The line on which letters sit is called the (1 mark)
   A. baseline
   B. descender line
   C. border
   D. ascender line

15. How many beats does a crotchet last? (1 mark)
   A. Half
   B. Two
   C. Four
   D. One

16. How many claps are there in the pattern ta-te ta-te taa (rest)? (1 mark)
   A. Three
   B. Four
   C. Six
   D. Five

17. How can you make a slab of even thickness? (1 mark)
   A. Drop it on the floor
   B. Squeeze with one hand
   C. Freeze it
   D. Roll the clay with a bottle between two sticks of equal thickness

18. Which nationality was Zoltan Kodaly, whose method uses hand signs? (1 mark)
   A. Chinese
   B. Brazilian
   C. Hungarian
   D. Kenyan

19. Pitch means (1 mark)
   A. how long a sound lasts
   B. the speed of a song
   C. how loud a sound is
   D. how high or low a sound is

20. Which describes a false start in a sprint? (1 mark)
   A. Finishing first
   B. Falling at the end
   C. Running in the wrong direction
   D. Moving before the last signal

21. When sprinting, where should your eyes look? (1 mark)
   A. Behind you
   B. Straight ahead
   C. At your feet
   D. At the sky

22. A relay race is a race in which (1 mark)
   A. people throw a ball
   B. one person runs all the way
   C. people jump into sand
   D. team members take turns running and pass a baton

23. A balance in gymnastics is (1 mark)
   A. a jump into water
   B. a fast run
   C. a throw
   D. a position held still for a few seconds

24. How can you fix sagging hips in the crab balance? (1 mark)
   A. Drop your head
   B. Lie down
   C. Bend your arms
   D. Push harder through your hands and feet

25. In a partner check for the crab balance, how many touching points does the table have? (1 mark)
   A. Six
   B. Eight
   C. Two
   D. Four

26. Which is a way to give good feedback to a partner? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh at their mistakes
   B. Say nothing
   C. Push them
   D. Say one thing that was good and one thing to improve

27. When singing, you should breathe (1 mark)
   A. by holding your breath
   B. deeply so your tummy moves out gently
   C. only through the ears
   D. by shouting

28. Which facial expression fits a joyful song? (1 mark)
   A. A smile
   B. A frown
   C. A yawn
   D. Closed eyes

29. Tempo means (1 mark)
   A. the name of the song
   B. the speed of the music
   C. the number of verses
   D. how loud the music is

30. In a folk song, the singer who leads is called the (1 mark)
   A. umpire
   B. drummer
   C. soloist
   D. listener

31. A sacred song is (1 mark)
   A. a work song only
   B. a song of worship
   C. a song with no words
   D. a song about a football match

32. Photos on a digital device are kept in its (1 mark)
   A. strap
   B. memory
   C. lens
   D. flash

33. Who should you ask before using a school digital device? (1 mark)
   A. A stranger
   B. A teacher or adult
   C. A friend's pet
   D. Nobody

34. How should you clean the lens of a camera? (1 mark)
   A. With water and sand
   B. With a soft, dry cloth
   C. With a stick
   D. With your fingers

35. Which note is played with the thumb hole and hole 1 covered? (1 mark)
   A. A
   B. G
   C. C
   D. B

36. Music is written on a (1 mark)
   A. table
   B. staff
   C. ruler
   D. wall

37. Indigenous games are (1 mark)
   A. games with no rules
   B. games from space
   C. traditional games that belong to a people and place
   D. games played only with computers

38. The snake slither is done (1 mark)
   A. hopping
   B. lying on the tummy and wriggling forward
   C. standing on tiptoe
   D. running fast

39. On which occasion may the national anthem be sung? (1 mark)
   A. Madaraka Day celebrations
   B. Only at night
   C. A private joke
   D. Never

40. A display portfolio holds (1 mark)
   A. your best finished works
   B. only rubbish
   C. only rough drafts
   D. tools

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain how to write a rhythm from dictation. (3 marks)

42. How can you show the mood of a joyful song when singing? (3 marks)

43. Why should we enter the water feet first? (2 marks)

44. Name four guide lines used for free hand lettering. (4 marks)

45. How do you care for a paint brush? (3 marks)

46. Write what the signs p and f mean. (2 marks)

47. Explain how a drum makes sound and how its parts work together. (5 marks)

48. Give four ways to make a clear centre of interest. (4 marks)

49. State four safety rules for the swimming pool. (4 marks)

50. Describe the game hawk and the chicks. (4 marks)

51. Why is colour classification important in painting? (2 marks)

52. Explain what tone or value means in a drawing. (3 marks)

53. What is the difference between a working portfolio and a display portfolio? (2 marks)

54. How should you behave when the Kenya National Anthem is sung? (3 marks)

55. State four safety rules for gymnastics. (4 marks)

56. Explain what sportsmanship means and give two examples. (3 marks)

57. Why is it important to warm up before doing gymnastics? (3 marks)

58. Explain why it is dangerous for a child to jump into a river to rescue someone. (3 marks)

59. Describe the sit-and-slide water entry. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Drum
   A drum is struck to make sound. The others are played by blowing.

2. B — pluck its metal tongues with your thumbs
   The kalimba or mbira has metal tongues that you pluck with the thumbs.

3. B — It vibrates and makes the sound
   The stretched skin shakes very fast and produces sound.

4. A — low notes
   Longer bars vibrate more slowly and sound lower.

5. B — The stick or hand that strikes it
   The beater is what hits the drumhead.

6. D — overhand knot
   The learner uses overhand knots to make the net around the core.

7. A — Goal Keeper
   GK is the Goal Keeper, a defender who guards the goal.

8. A — 0.9 metres
   A defender must stand at least 0.9 metres away.

9. B — Flour paste
   Flour mixed with water and heated water makes a paste.

10. D — Black
   Black makes a shade, a darker tone.

11. D — White
   White makes a tint, a lighter tone.

12. D — One beat
   A crotchet rest is one beat of silence.

13. A — Variation of note values
   Good patterns vary the note values.

14. A — baseline
   All letters sit on the baseline.

15. D — One
   A crotchet lasts for one beat.

16. D — Five
   Ta-te has two, ta-te has two, taa has one, and the rest has none, so five claps.

17. D — Roll the clay with a bottle between two sticks of equal thickness
   Equal sticks on both sides keep the slab even.

18. C — Hungarian
   Zoltan Kodaly was a Hungarian music teacher.

19. D — how high or low a sound is
   Pitch is the highness or lowness of a note.

20. D — Moving before the last signal
   A false start is leaving before the start signal.

21. B — Straight ahead
   Keeping the head up and eyes ahead helps balance and speed.

22. D — team members take turns running and pass a baton
   In a relay, runners pass a baton to the next teammate.

23. D — a position held still for a few seconds
   A balance is a still position that you hold under control.

24. D — Push harder through your hands and feet
   Pushing through hands and feet lifts the hips.

25. D — Four
   The table has four legs, two hands and two feet.

26. D — Say one thing that was good and one thing to improve
   Kind and helpful feedback includes praise and a suggestion.

27. B — deeply so your tummy moves out gently
   Deep breathing supports the voice.

28. A — A smile
   Facial expressions show the mood.

29. B — the speed of the music
   Tempo is how fast or slow.

30. C — soloist
   The soloist sings the lead part.

31. B — a song of worship
   Sacred songs praise God, give thanks or teach faith.

32. B — memory
   Digital photos are stored in memory.

33. B — A teacher or adult
   Always get permission.

34. B — With a soft, dry cloth
   A soft cloth cleans without scratching.

35. D — B
   B uses the thumb and the first hole.

36. B — staff
   The staff has five lines and four spaces.

37. C — traditional games that belong to a people and place
   They are passed on by playing together.

38. B — lying on the tummy and wriggling forward
   The body moves side to side like a snake.

39. A — Madaraka Day celebrations
   It is sung on national days and at official events.

40. A — your best finished works
   It is for showing to others.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen twice to the pattern. Count the beats. For each beat decide if it was one long sound, two short sounds or silence, and write taa, ta-te or a rest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Smile, use lively gestures, sing brightly and at a lively tempo.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is safer because you cannot hit your head on the bottom, and you can see where you land.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ascender line, top of small letters, baseline and descender line.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each line.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rinse when changing colour, wash with soap after use, shape the tip and store it flat or with hairs up. Never leave it standing on its hairs in water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: p means soft. f means loud.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: The beater or hand strikes the drumhead, which vibrates and makes the sound. The hollow shell makes the sound fuller and louder. The ropes hold the skin tight, and a tighter skin gives a higher sound.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for striking, vibrating skin, shell, ropes, and effect of tightness on pitch.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide the subject first; move closer; remove distractions; place the subject in the middle or slightly to the side; keep it sharp; bend to eye level. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Swim only when watched; never swim alone; walk on the pool side; no pushing; no diving in shallow water; follow the whistle. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: A hen stands in front and chicks hold on behind in a line. A hawk tries to tag the last chick. The hen spreads her arms and blocks. When the last chick is tagged, roles change.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid part.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps us know which colours to mix to get others. It shows that only primary colours are needed to make all the other colours.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tone means how light or dark an area is. In a charcoal drawing, we can make tones from light grey to black by pressing lightly or hard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for lightness or darkness, 1 mark for range of tones, 1 mark for charcoal pressure.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: A working portfolio holds work in progress. A display portfolio holds the best finished works for showing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stand straight and still, face the flag, remove your cap, sing clearly and do not talk or play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use a mat or soft ground; keep the space clear; remove jewellery; tie back long hair; warm up; take turns; stop if there is pain. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Being fair and kind in sports. Examples: following the rules and shaking hands with the other team.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for each example.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Warm-up prepares the muscles and joints, prevents injury and helps you perform better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: The child may also drown because water can be deep or fast. It is safer to shout for an adult and throw something that floats.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the danger, 2 marks for the safe action.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sit on the edge with feet in the water, hands on the edge beside the hips. Turn to face the wall and slide gently into the water holding the edge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.
